summary: An excerpt from a fiction work ("Book 14 — part 7") in which the narrator, who is on the run, recounts a last conversation with a friend nicknamed Wheeze, who is also leaving town after the FBI raided the squat where Wheeze and Wilson had been living. The narrator worries about losing Wheeze and then turns to finding where his brother Wilson has been taken. The passage closes with a backstory of Wilson as a protective older brother, including a memorable wedding escape on Lake Minnetonka and Wilson's later punishment and wayward path.
one_line: A fugitive narrator says goodbye to his friend Wheeze, then reflects on his protective older brother Wilson and the search for him.
key_facts: The narrator crashed the night after the FBI raid at Wilson's house, a home Wilson and friends had been squatting in for two years.
The house had been foreclosed, and Wilson and his friends moved in as a protest; the bank never came to evict them.
The FBI showed up at the squat, and the narrator realized they would be looking for him too.
The narrator's friend Wheeze says "I'm heading out" and the two agree to "Keep in touch" through a secure communication method.
Wheeze is described as smart and funny, and as someone who would take a bug outside and let it go to avoid squashing it.
The narrator says he had to find out where they had taken his brother.
Wilson held the narrator's hand when he was afraid and carried him when he got tired.
At a big wedding on Lake Minnetonka, a drunken uncle spouted racist things, and Wilson dragged the narrator out the back door before he could lose it.
The stepmother frowned at the narrator and said "don't you dare" without speaking aloud.
The brothers took a canoe into the middle of the lake without life jackets and went swimming in their underwear.
The narrator had to save up for months to pay for the ugly dress that was ruined during the swim.
After the wedding incident, Wilson was sent to a summer boot camp for troublemakers, where he learned to pick locks and steal cars.
Wilson finished high school and left home, and the narrator wanted to follow him.
